prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: Basically, a strategy I used during this game consisted of identifying each character through symbolism. For instance, for the characters, if one had purple hair to the right and black shoes, I would identify it as "purple right, black shoes." I only changed my strategy when the non-characters showed and that was generally through looking at what the characteristic is showing.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: I think some mistakes were shown in the non-character section. For instance, the black cubes and the way some of the shapes were kicking up, I kept mistaking it for kicking or jumping when me and my partner didn't write the names for those. Also, I did get some typos wrong. Instead of saying grey square, I said white square instead.

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: We both kinda suggested the names. My partner did take the lead, but I was recommending some typical names that could be obvious for us to incorporate throughout the characters so we can get points.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: Ok, so for the first 3 rounds, we decided to use the colours of the hair and the direction it was facing - added the colour of the arms and feet when they were getting more inconsistent with shapes. Overall, we kept the same strategy. Instead of actually using for example orange left red brown we made it simpler: olrb and it was working very good. For the last round we kept the directions strategy, but it was much harder, so if the head of the figuring was central, we used central and then whichever side was sticking out more - center left. It was much difficult because there was not a obvious pattern and some were repeating. Overall, it was very interesting and I really enjoyed it.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake

prompt_mistake.value: Yes, one of them was a typo, I do not remember the round, maybe 2nd or 3rd, but I  think it was the only one that we got wrong before 4. However, I made some mistakes in the 4th round because, as previously mentioned, there was not a very obvious pattern so I wrote the direction I thought was agreed upon.

Then, I suggested we should use abbreviations, like orbb instead of orange right black brown as it woud be easier. My partner was nice ehought to write all of them.

prompt_strategy.value: We would look at each image together and tell each other what we saw from our own POV and try to collaborate on a simple way for us to remember the image in 1-2 words. prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: At first, we tried to write down the characteristics of the image with whole words, but it became hard as the rounds went by. We then switched our strategy to initials based on the color of the hair, hands and feet, and from there everything went great. The last round was a bit tricky because we changed the strategy again based on the action of  the image. Overall, we did well.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: We looked at each figure and described it, from the head to the feet. The first set of characters were minions so we called them minions and used something else to differentiate each one. We also chose not to include the description "black hand," we only added the color hands if it was something apart from black. the color of shoes was also a distinguishing feature, so we added that for each figure, too. The third test was quite tricky so we chose to keep up the method we used earlier regardless of the height of the minion. The final test was the most challenging since the character took different postures. What we did was to choose a name for each posture and call every character by a specific name. It was fun brainstorming with my partner and she made the discussion captivating.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: Yes we made mistakes. At first, we didn't take note that the spaces between words were also counted. Then we also had spelling errors once or twice.

prompt_working_together.name: working_together

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: We chose how to name them and suggested names together.
